promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The Spoken Language Endorsement: assessment and grading

questions.q: Which component of the Pearson Edexcel GCSE English Language (1EN0) qualification is the Spoken Language Endorsement?
options: Component 1
Component 2
Component 3
Component 4
questions.explain: The Spoken Language Endorsement is Component 3 of the Edexcel GCSE English Language specification.

questions.q: How does the Spoken Language Endorsement contribute to the overall 9-1 GCSE grade?
options: It counts for 20% of the final grade
It counts for 10% of the final grade
It does not contribute to the 9-1 grade and is reported separately
It counts for 40% of the final grade
questions.explain: The endorsement is reported separately on the certificate and does not form part of the numerical 9-1 grade.

questions.q: Which of the following are the possible grades a student can be awarded for the Spoken Language Endorsement?
options: Pass, Merit or Distinction
Grades 9 to 1
A* to G
Fail, Pass or Credit
questions.explain: The endorsement is graded Pass, Merit or Distinction (or Not Classified if no evidence is provided).

questions.q: Who is responsible for assessing a student's spoken language performance for the endorsement?
options: An external Pearson examiner
The student's own teacher (teacher assessment)
A visiting moderator on the day
Another student in a peer assessment
questions.explain: The endorsement is assessed by the student's teacher, with samples monitored by Pearson.

questions.q: What form of spoken task must a student complete for the Edexcel Spoken Language Endorsement?
options: A group debate only
A formal individual presentation followed by questions
A recorded telephone conversation
A written speech submitted on paper
questions.explain: Students prepare and deliver a formal individual presentation and then respond to questions on it.

questions.q: Which variety of English are students required to use effectively in the presentation?
options: Regional dialect
Spoken Standard English
Informal slang
Written academic English
questions.explain: AO9 requires the effective use of spoken Standard English in speeches and presentations.

questions.q: The Spoken Language Endorsement assesses three assessment objectives numbered AO7, AO8 and AO9. What does AO7 focus on?
options: Listening and responding to spoken language
Demonstrating presentation skills in a formal setting
Using spoken Standard English
Analysing a poem's structure
questions.explain: AO7 requires students to demonstrate presentation skills in a formal setting.

questions.q: Which assessment objective covers listening and responding appropriately to questions and feedback on a presentation?
options: AO7
AO8
AO9
AO5
questions.explain: AO8 covers listening and responding appropriately to spoken language, including questions and feedback.

questions.q: Why is planning the structure of a presentation important for meeting AO7?
options: It guarantees a Distinction automatically
It helps deliver ideas clearly and coherently in a formal setting
It removes the need to answer questions
It allows the student to read from a full script word for word
questions.explain: A clear structure supports the coherent, effective delivery of ideas that AO7 rewards.

questions.q: A student wants to engage the audience during a formal presentation. Which technique best supports effective delivery?
options: Reading the whole talk from a script with no eye contact
Using varied tone, pace and eye contact with the audience
Speaking as quietly and quickly as possible
Using slang to seem more relatable
questions.explain: Varying vocal delivery and maintaining eye contact are effective techniques for engaging an audience formally.

questions.q: Which of these best demonstrates effective use of spoken Standard English in a presentation?
options: Frequent filler words and slang throughout
Clear, grammatically accurate speech with appropriate vocabulary
Reciting memorised text with no expression
Using only very short simple sentences
questions.explain: Effective spoken Standard English is grammatically accurate and uses vocabulary suited to a formal setting.

questions.q: After a presentation, a listener asks a challenging question. What is the most appropriate response to meet AO8?
options: Ignore the question and repeat the presentation
Listen carefully and give a relevant, considered answer
Answer with a single unrelated word
Refuse to respond because it was not planned
questions.explain: AO8 rewards listening and responding appropriately and relevantly to questions.

questions.q: Why does the endorsement include a question-and-answer element after the presentation?
options: To fill time in the lesson
To assess spontaneous listening and responding skills (AO8)
To let the audience grade the speaker
To test the student's reading comprehension
questions.explain: The question-and-answer stage allows assessment of a student's ability to listen and respond appropriately to spoken language.

questions.q: Which of the following would most likely lower the effectiveness of a formal presentation?
options: Signposting the main points clearly
Using appropriate formal register
Mumbling and turning away from the audience
Adapting language to suit the audience
questions.explain: Poor audibility and lack of audience contact weaken the formal delivery AO7 assesses.

questions.q: If a student provides no evidence of spoken language performance, how is the endorsement reported?
options: As a Pass by default
As Not Classified
As a Grade 1
The whole GCSE is withheld
questions.explain: Where there is no assessable evidence, the endorsement is reported as Not Classified.

questions.q: A student is preparing a presentation on climate change for the endorsement. Which preparation choice best fits the formal setting required by AO7?
options: Writing bullet-point cue cards and rehearsing aloud
Deciding to improvise entirely with no preparation
Preparing only informal jokes with friends
Planning to read silently to the class
questions.explain: Cue cards and rehearsal support confident, structured formal delivery without reading a full script.

questions.q: During questions, a student is asked something they had not anticipated. Which approach best demonstrates AO8?
options: Pausing to think, then giving a clear and relevant answer
Saying they cannot answer any unplanned questions
Changing the subject to their rehearsed material
Answering in a regional dialect to save time
questions.explain: Taking a moment to think and then responding clearly and relevantly shows effective listening and responding.

questions.q: A student tends to use slang and fillers when nervous. To strengthen AO9 in the presentation, they should focus on:
options: Adding more slang to sound natural
Practising clear, formal, grammatically accurate speech
Speaking as fast as possible to finish quickly
Avoiding eye contact to reduce nerves
questions.explain: AO9 rewards effective spoken Standard English, so practising formal, accurate speech directly addresses the weakness.

questions.q: A teacher is deciding whether a student's performance merits a Distinction rather than a Pass. They should judge the work against:
options: The number of slides used
The graded criteria for presentation, responding and Standard English
How long the presentation lasted in minutes
The student's written coursework
questions.explain: The endorsement grade is decided against the criteria covering AO7, AO8 and AO9, not surface features such as slide count.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE English Language (1EN0) specification; Component 3: Spoken Language Endorsement
